q-99063.name: Question 1
q-99063.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{4}{x}?$
q-99063.worked_solution:
To plot $y=\frac{4}{x},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=\frac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/b3a79a8dbe82342c0ab1e16371f8c1d82833f4ebc3bad659f1a619ab1e92733e.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\frac{4}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/e10be40920aebaaf2f5984e25cff2143ee145851d5feaef48df883cf3556cacc.png)

q-98004.name: Question 5
q-98004.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2(x+1)}?$
q-98004.worked_solution:
To plot $y=\frac{1}{2(x+1)},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=\frac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/a32495fcca947d01cf8d3218fc5cfc0cce083a34e6fb6b629d92ba9e47039a6e.png)

- Translate it by $1$ unit to the left to get the graph of $y=\frac{1}{x+1}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/049f9c306c007026bc72e5f00d925cf22d80d94049aa82e3c81d7fc7c289249f.png)

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2(x+1)}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/c52f568868328061237d43e4650180321ec4a40e886a62f4a678f0276afe821b.png)

q-270753.name: Question 8
q-270753.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/84c4df89c98cd103049ac6161c5d3e4eec258d3ecb3c1af94bf7d300f9342d22.png)

The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What are the values of $a,$ $b,$ and $k?$

$a=$
{{field-1}},$\,b=$
{{field-2}},$\,k=$
{{field-3}}
q-270753.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=1.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=-1.$ This means that $k=1.5$ and $b=-1,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x-(-1)}+1.5=\frac{a}{x+1}+1.5.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(1,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x+1}+1.5 \\ 3.5 & =\frac{a}{1+1}+1.5 \\ 2 & =\frac{a}{2} \\ a & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-113475.name: Question 9
q-113475.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/fc0ad365fca91e61da2e7f09197299ea6130018d7490873d3568231be360b481.png)

The diagram above shows the graph of $y=\frac{a}{x}.$ What is the value of $a?$
q-113475.worked_solution:
Notice that the point $(3,-1)$ lies on the graph.

Substituting its coordinates into the equation $y=\frac{a}{x},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}-1=\frac{a}{3}\,⟹\,a=-3.\end{aligned}
$$
